title_as_listed: Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Multi-Function Air Fryer Toaster Oven | Countertop Convection Cooker, 24 One-Touch Preset Options, Extra Large Interior, Six Cooking Accessories Included

editorial.dek: A real countertop oven — French doors and an extra-large interior — and the biggest cavity in the shop.
editorial.best_for: Baking, roasting, and cooking for more than four
editorial.catch: 26.5 lb and 16.9 inches deep. It is the heaviest and the largest thing here, and it needs the most counter and the most cleaning.
check_before_buying: Measure depth against the listed 16.9" and check the cabinet clearance above it, not just the footprint.
Count the presets you will actually use. The listing disagrees with itself on how many there are — 24 in the title, 25 in the bullet copy (FLG-020) — so read the number on the page in front of you.
Budget for the accessories — the listing counts them as six in its title and seven in its bullet copy (FLG-010), and more parts means more to wash.

blocking_questions.question: Did the five people-supplied links mean these five products, or were they placeholders?
blocking_questions.answer: No — the supplied tokens do not identify products, and they were never meant to. Each token is 9 characters; an ASIN is a 10-character code, so a token cannot be one. The mapping in this register is what the links resolve to, recorded live on five separate occasions, four of which reproduced the mapping exactly (5/5 each time). The fifth, on 2026-11-20, saw one token land on the Amazon homepage instead of its recorded listing — logged as FLG-030, which neither confirms nor invalidates the mapping. Nothing public binds the short code to a product, so the intended fields stay blank and the observed target is kept in its own column. The intended fields are settled as “unknown”, which is a settled answer, not a gap in the record.

redirect_observation.note: The <title> says 26QT / six accessories; the products.json title field (from the listing body) says 26QT capacity and 7 accessories. Accessory count differs between title and bullet copy on the same page — logged as FLG-010.

listing_conflicts.note: Accessory count: the page title says 'Six Cooking Accessories Included'; the bullet copy in the same read said '7 Accessories Included'. This site does not pick one — it links the listing and states both.

Preset count: the page title says '24 One-Touch Preset Options'; the bullet list on the same page says '25 COOKING PRE-SETS' and then names eleven modes (ribs, defrost, bake, toast, chicken, pizza, pastry, slow cook, roast, reheat, keep warm). Neither number is used as a headline on this site.

Serving claim: the bullet copy says the 26-quart cavity is 'suitable for preparing food for 4–6 people', can rotisserie a 6-lb chicken and bake a 12" pizza. That is the manufacturer's own sizing claim on the listing, quoted as such.

faq: Is it an air fryer or an oven?

The listing describes both: a 26-quart French-door air fryer toaster oven whose bullets name cooking modes including toast, ribs, slow cook and roast. Its details table lists 16.9"D x 15.8"W x 14.8"H and a capacity of 24.6 liters.
How many presets and accessories does it come with?

The listing disagrees with itself. The page title says 24 one-touch preset options and six cooking accessories, while the bullet heading says 25 cooking pre-sets, and an earlier capture of the same page read 7 accessories. Both readings are published on the Flagged for review page; this site picks neither (FLG-010, FLG-020).
How large a cook can it handle?

The listing's own bullet says the 26-quart cavity is sized for 4-6 people, can rotisserie a 6-lb chicken and bake a 12-inch pizza. That is the seller's sizing claim on the listing, quoted as a claim and not as advice from this desk (FLG-021).
